rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant covered prophethood and more, not only God's lordship, supporting the preceding argument.
rows.anchor: دلالة على أن الميثاق لم يؤخذ على الربوبية فحسب بل على النبوة وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: God's proof encompasses all creatures; He took them at the covenant and demonstrated this by closing his hand.
rows.anchor: سألت أبا عبد الله عن قول الله { وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم } قال نعم لله الحجة على جميع خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai reads the taking here as encompassing and ownership.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الرواية أنها تفسر الأخذ في الآية بمعنى الإحاطة والملك

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The covenant was witnessed directly; knowledge was fixed, its scene forgotten, and some affirmed verbally without inward faith.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسكان عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قوله { وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This sound report refutes those who deny an actual primordial covenant and interpret the witness as merely learning signs of lordship.
rows.anchor: والرواية ترد على منكري دلالة الآية على أخذ الميثاق في الذر تفسيرهم قوله

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far recounts his father's account of Adam's clay being kneaded with sweet and bitter water, producing tiny descendants divided into right and left groups and tested by entry into fire.
rows.anchor: عن زرارة أن رجلا سأل أبا جعفر عليه السلام عن قول الله عز وجل { وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم } إلى آخر الآية، فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order to enter the fire is a metaphor for entering servitude and obedience.
rows.anchor: وكأن الأمر بدخول النار كناية عن الدخول في حظيرة العبودية والانقياد للطاعة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: God formed those He loved from paradise clay and those He hated from fire clay, then sent them in the shadow-world with prophets; their acknowledgment of God and the Imams' authority followed their divine love or hatred.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال إن الله عز وجل خلق الخلق فخلق من أحب مما أحب فكان ما أحب أن خلقه من طينة الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shadow-world described by the Imams is this world in one respect and another world in another, with some rules like worldly life and others unlike it.
rows.anchor: وقد تكرر ذكر الظلال في لسان أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام والمراد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ayyashi's addition that the answer occurred in the covenant is the narrator's explanation, not the Imam's wording.
rows.anchor: وما زاده العياشي من كلام الراوي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Asked how tiny particles could answer, the Imam says God made them such that they would answer when questioned.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير قال قلت لأبي عبد الله عليه السلام كيف أجابوا وهم ذر؟ قال جعل فيهم ما إذا سألهم أجابوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report does not mean their condition merely signaled the answer; their eventual worldly speech explains how the answer was possible.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد بقوله " جعل فيهم ما إذا سألهم أجابوه " دلالة حالهم على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Imam's wording says they answer when asked, not merely if they happen to speak, supporting a real exchange.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده قوله عليه السلام ما إذا سألهم، ولم يقل ما لو تكلموا ونحو ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The descendants affirmed God's lordship with their tongues and hearts; when asked where they were, the Imam replied that God made them in a form sufficient for this.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قول الله { ألست بربكم } قالوا بألسنتهم؟ قال نعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that realm tongue and heart were one, so the verbal affirmation was true and accompanied by the heart; God created them in a way that made questioning and answering possible.
rows.anchor: القلب هناك واحد، ولذلك قال عليه السلام نعم وبقلوبهم فصدق اللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports explicitly establish that the address and speech in the verse are literal, not figurative.
rows.anchor: صريح في أن التكليم والتكلم في الآية على الحقيقة دون المجاز بل هي صريحة فيه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet describes right and left groups affirming God's lordship, being mixed, returned to Adam's loins, and assigned their eventual homes; an interlocutor asks why they were mixed.
rows.anchor: فخلط بعضهم ببعض فقال قائل منهم رب لم خلطت بيننا؟ قال ولهم أعمال من دون ذلك هم لها عاملون

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Asked what people should do, the Prophet replies that each group performs deeds suited to its dwelling.
rows.anchor: فقال قائل يا رسول الله فما الأعمال؟ قال يعمل كل قوم لمنازلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's phrase about the Throne over water denotes that the covenant-taking preceded what follows, not that souls existed temporally before bodies as many proponents of the atom-world suppose.
rows.anchor: كناية عن تقدم أخذ الميثاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each eventual home calls for fitting worldly deeds: the people of Paradise do good and those of Hell do evil; inviting people to good remains meaningful even with a settled destination, as 2:148 shows.
rows.anchor: أي إن كل واحد من المنزلين يحتاج إلى أعمال تناسبه في الدنيا فإن كان العامل من أهل الجنة عمل الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no conflict between bliss or misery being determined relative to complete causes and remaining undetermined relative to human choice, which is itself only a partial cause; the author refers back to 7:29–30.
rows.anchor: ولا منافاة بين تعين السعادة والشقاوة بالنظر إلى العلل التامة وبين عدم تعينها بالنظر إلى اختيار الإنسان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God took Adam's covenant, recorded his lifespan, provision, and afflictions, then brought his descendants out like tiny particles and took their covenant too.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله { وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم } الآية قال خلق الله آدم وأخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas's many versions vary in wording but share the extraction of Adam's descendants and their covenant as their core meaning.
rows.anchor: وقد روي هذا المعنى عن ابن عباس بطرق كثيرة في ألفاظ مختلفة لكن الجميع تشترك في أصل المعنى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
rows.claim: A report says God drew white descendants from Adam's right and dark descendants from his left, declared their destinations, took their covenant, and made them witnesses so they could not plead ignorance or inherited shirk; it links this to 3:83 and 6:149.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة الهمداني عن ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The atom-covenant report is transmitted in both suspended and connected forms from many Companions and Imams through Sunni and Shi'a routes, making a claim of semantic mass-transmission plausible.
rows.anchor: وقد روى حديث الذر كما في الرواية موقوفة وموصولة عن عدة من أصحاب رسول الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Qatada, a Companion, reports the Prophet saying God created Adam and drew creation from his back, some destined for Paradise and some for Hell; the continuation asks what deeds people should perform.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرحمان بن قتادة السلمي وكان من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: When asked what to do after hearing that some were destined for Paradise and others for Hell, the Prophet answers: act according to the sites of destiny.
rows.anchor: فقال رجل يا رسول الله فعلى ماذا نعمل؟ قال على مواقع القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's answer does not cancel choice: God decreed outcomes through our choices, so deeds remain ours while occurring in accordance with decree.
rows.anchor: فأجابه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بأن هذا قدر منه تعالى وأن أعمالنا في عين أنا نعملها وهي منسوبة إلينا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far explains that the human fitra is innate knowledge of God; he says the descendants were brought from Adam like particles, shown God, and thereby came to know their Lord.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال سألته عن قول الله عز وجل { حنفاء لله غير مشركين }

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says every newborn is born with fitra, meaning knowledge that God is the child's Creator, and the author connects this to the Qur'anic statement that people identify God as creator.
rows.anchor: وقال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits the middle of Zurarah's report in the same wording, supporting the author's account of the verse's literal witnessing and address against those who deny it.
rows.anchor: وروي وسط الحديث العياشي في تفسيره عن زرارة بعين اللفظ

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: In a version transmitted in al-Ma'ani, Abu Ja'far's wording is that God showed them His creation rather than Himself.
rows.anchor: عن زرارة عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام إلا أنه قال فعرفهم وأراهم صنعه بدل قوله فعرفهم وأراهم نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai suspects that the alternate wording was deliberately paraphrased to avoid an imagined implication of corporeality; he calls the change corrupting and prefers the wording in al-Kafi and al-Ayyashi, which has no connection to corporeality.
rows.anchor: ولعله من تغيير اللفظ قصدا للنقل بالمعنى زعما أن ظاهر اللفظ يوهم التجسم وفيه إفساد اللفظ والمعنى جميعا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Zurarah reports that knowledge was fixed in people's hearts, they forgot the covenant scene but will recall it, and otherwise no one would know their Creator and Provider.
rows.anchor: عن ابن بكير عن زرارة قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن قول الله { وإذ أخذ ربك } الآية قال ثبتت المعرفة في قلوبهم

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn saw no objection to coitus interruptus, citing the covenant: everyone from whom God took a covenant will emerge, even if conceived on a hard stone.
rows.anchor: قال كان علي بن الحسين عليه السلام لا يرى بالعزل بأسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that the report is also transmitted from Ali ibn al-Husayn by Ibn Abi Shayba and Ibn Jarir, and that a similar report is attributed to the Prophet through Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.
rows.anchor: وروى هذا المعنى أيضا عن سعيد بن منصور وابن مردويه عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the reports about the primordial realm are so numerous, the author omits most after citing enough to convey their meaning and reserves reports about the prophets' covenant for another section.
rows.anchor: وأعلم أن الروايات في الذر كثيرة جدا وقد تركنا إيراد أكثرها لوفاء ما أوردنا من ذلك بمعناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhar' means creation. Hell as the outcome for many humans and jinn does not contradict the statement that creation aims at mercy and Paradise in 11:119, because 'goal' can describe different stages of an act.
rows.anchor: الذرء هو الخلق، وقد عرف الله سبحانه جهنم غاية لخلق كثير من الجن والإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The carpenter's goal has a primary, perfected end—the completed door—and a necessary secondary end: unusable wood becomes waste; the farmer's seed likewise partly yields grain and partly goes to waste.
rows.anchor: فللنجار في صنع الباب بالنسبة إلى الأخشاب التي بين يديه نوعان من الغاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's original, perfected aim in creating humans is to show them mercy and admit them to Paradise; Hell is a derivative and necessary outcome for those whose acquired capacities lead them to ruin, which God wills secondarily.
rows.anchor: وصح أن لله سبحانه غاية في خلقه الإنسان مثلا وهو أن يشملهم برحمته ويدخلهم جنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hearts, eyes, and ears described as unable to perceive indicate that these people have lost the capacity to receive divine mercy; signs, true admonition, and innate evidence no longer benefit them.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى بطلأن استعدادهم للوقوع في مجرى الرحمة الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their organs are not naturally defective; God seals their faculties in requital because they first changed the path of servitude, as 30:30 and 8:53 explain.
rows.anchor: ولا يفسد عقل ولا عين ولا أذن في عمله وقد خلقها الله لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cattle comparison concludes that they have lost the human ability, through hearing, sight, and heart, to distinguish good from evil and benefit from harm for a happy human life.
rows.anchor: فإنهم فقدوا ما يتميز به الإنسان من سائر الحيوان، وهو تمييز الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are compared specifically with grazing cattle because eating and sex precede other animal aims; appetitive powers are primary, while anger and repulsion serve them.
rows.anchor: لأن التمتع بالأكل والسفاد أقدم وأسبق بالنسبة إلى الطبع الحيواني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links the comparison with cattle to 47:12: animals are only relatively astray, since their nature guides them to their intended animal happiness and they are not blameworthy.
rows.anchor: والذين كفروا يتمتعون ويأكلون كما تأكل الأنعام والنار مثوى لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are more astray and blameworthy because they possess faculties suited to human happiness but squander them and use them only for bodily pleasures like cattle.
rows.anchor: لكنهم أفسدوها وضيعوا أعمالها ونزلوها منزلة السمع والبصر والقلب التي في الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their true heedlessness is another consequence of God's sealing their hearts, eyes, and ears; heedlessness is the source of every error and falsehood.
rows.anchor: حقيقة الغفلة هي التي توجد عندهم فإنها بمشيئة الله سبحانه، ألبسها

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Rida recounts that Bal'am ibn Ba'ura, given God's supreme name and answered when invoking it, sided with Pharaoh against Moses; his donkey refused to pursue the prophet and believers, so he beat it to death and lost the name from his tongue.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الحسن الرضا عليه السلام أنه أعطي بلعم ابن باعورا الإسم الأعظم، وكان يدعو به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Imam's phrase about a parable apparently refers to the story of Bal'am; the author postpones discussion of the supreme name to his treatment of the divine names.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنه يشير إلى نبأ بلعم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud identifies the person stripped of God's signs as an Israelite called Bal'am ibn Abur.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود في قوله { واتل عليهم نبأ الذي آتيناه آياتنا فانسلخ منها }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies him as Bal'am ibn Ba'ura, also called Bal'am ibn Amir, who had received the supreme name and lived among the Israelites.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال هو بلعم بن باعوراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports from sources besides Ibn Abbas also call him Bal'am and make him an Israelite, while other details about him are transmitted as well.
rows.anchor: وقد روي كون اسمه بلعم وكونه من بني إسرائيل عن غير ابن عباس

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: Al-Ruh al-Ma'ani reports a view that the passage concerned Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt, who hoped to be the promised messenger but left after the Prophet recited Ya Sin, saying he would consider the matter.
rows.anchor: وفي روح المعاني عند ذكر القول بأن الآية نزلت في أمية بن أبي الصلت الثقفي الشاعر إنه كان قرأ الكتب القديمة
